meetings.headline: Committee met its energy-reduction goal but remains stalled awaiting building energy audits needed for Turkey Hill decisions.
meetings.summary: The Green Community Task Force reviewed its FY26 annual energy report, which showed the town hit its energy-reduction goal, with Turkey Hill and the old elementary building flagged as the largest energy users. Most of the meeting covered stalled progress: a National Grid building-energy audit and analysis six months overdue, no reserve fund for future LED streetlight maintenance, an unsuccessful styrofoam-recycling grant push, and broader town indecision on Turkey Hill, Town Hall and other building needs. No substantive votes were taken beyond routine approval of minutes and adjournment; the group discussed renaming itself an energy/sustainability committee and pursuing Tyler's appointment to a soon-open seat.

budget_items.topic: Streetlight savings and a proposed maintenance reserve fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said savings from lower streetlight bills have just been absorbed into the general budget with nothing set aside for future LED maintenance, and discussed creating a reserve or special revolving fund instead.
A member said the town badly needs an experienced grant writer, and noted a budgeted grant-writer line had gone unspent before.

budget_items.topic: PPP energy audit and comprehensive building analysis (CBA)
budget_items.what_was_said: National Grid was to provide a free preliminary audit and a comprehensive building analysis of all twelve town buildings, but the committee said it has waited months with no result.

budget_items.topic: Capital outlay override for building projects
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described how the town of Ashby used a one-time capital outlay override to fund and pay off building projects in a single year, and suggested Lunenburg consider it for its aging buildings.
A member said current incentives make an electric riding mower roughly half the price of an equivalent gas model, but the town would need duplicate equipment for separate departments.

budget_items.topic: Capital planning equipment list / mower purchase
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the school department's capital plan includes buying a new zero-turn mower and the group discussed pushing for an electric model.

A member relayed that capital planning discussed a perceived risk that hybrid police vehicle batteries could be costly once out of warranty, and that gas vehicle quotes may be sought for the next replacement round.

decisions.decision: Committee agreed to consider renaming itself from a Green Community committee toward something like an Energy or Energy and Sustainability Committee.
A member agreed to update the committee's Facebook page with the annual energy report the chair would send.
Chair agreed to push for Tyler's official appointment to an upcoming open committee seat.
Next meeting set for roughly mid-January, once the PPP building audit results are available.

meetings.headline: No quorum was reached; members informally discussed heat pump, solar and geothermal grant projects
meetings.summary: The Green Community Task Force never reached a quorum, so no official business or votes occurred; present members had an informal conversation about past and possible energy projects. They discussed the mini-split heat pump project at the schools (framed as both AC and heat, which unlocked grant funding), geothermal well drilling at another school, frustration over losing track of Turkey Hill's solar panel savings after the installer went out of business, predatory solar sales tactics, whether the town's ground-mount solar bylaw needs updating, and the group's ongoing push to get town departments to seek grant money before requesting town meeting funds. The meeting ended without a quorum and without any votes.

budget_items.topic: Mini-split heat pumps as a heat source
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said using mini-splits as a heat source, not just AC, was what enabled the project to qualify for free (grant) money. Getting the school administration to see the heating benefit, not just cooling, was described as a struggle.

budget_items.topic: Comparing mini-split cost to fossil fuel heating
budget_items.what_was_said: A member argued that when a building considers full electrification, the town should also be shown a traditional fossil-fuel cost comparison so voters can make an informed choice.

budget_items.topic: Geothermal wells at a school (state-pushed option)
budget_items.what_was_said: The state was said to be pushing geothermal; a school the size of the middle-high school reportedly drilled a large number of wells, and a member questioned what the return on investment would be.

A member said solar credits from Turkey Hill's panels are going somewhere and could fund the building's electricity so taxes don't rise as much, but the group has lost access to records of what the panels have actually saved since the installer went out of business.

The group discussed whether the town's ground-mount solar bylaw, which capped systems at a certain size, needs updating since panel efficiency has risen and the old cap now limits how much of a home's usage can be offset. They agreed it was worth looking into but did not resolve it.

budget_items.topic: Grant money vs. town-meeting funding requests
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described the task force's ongoing push to get the new town manager, select board, schools, and other town facilities to check with them for available grant/free money before putting funding requests on a town meeting warrant.

budget_items.topic: Next Green Communities grant round projects
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force said it is struggling to identify projects for the next spring grant round, after the mini-split project.

decisions.decision: Members agreed the town's ground-mount solar system size bylaw likely needs to be reviewed, without settling on a change.

meetings.headline: Green committee will pursue a townwide Mass Save building-assessment study before its next grant push
meetings.summary: The chair recapped a Mass Save Summit he attended, walking the task force through weatherization, heat-pump, building-management and electric-lawn-equipment incentive programs, plus new "portfolio prioritization" and building-assessment studies meant to get town buildings grant-ready. The group agreed to schedule a meeting with National Grid/Mass Save and the facilities director to start the portfolio study, put the Turkey Hill project on hold until then, reviewed the town's Green Community history and open incentive programs, and closed with brief updates on a styrofoam-recycling grant, school HVAC work, committee term expirations, and a motion on prior minutes.

meetings.headline: Committee pressed the schools and town to actually use already-approved, no-cost green energy grant funding.
meetings.summary: The Green Community Task Force reviewed the status of school and town energy projects funded through incentives, grants, and the capital plan, with no town money required for several of them, and pushed the school facilities director and other town departments to move faster. The committee also discussed member appointment and term-length irregularities, recruited prospective new members, and adjourned by roll-call vote after setting its next meeting for July.

budget_items.what_was_said: Equipment for the school HVAC system is on site and installation will begin once school ends; the school committee already voted to fund the district's portion, though the state/grant funding doesn't kick in until July 1.

Two refrigeration projects and a controls project were approved with no town dollar contribution, funded entirely through Unitil incentives and the Green Grant; the chair wants the facilities director to move faster since it costs the town nothing.

budget_items.what_was_said: HVAC upgrades at Town Hall and Ritter were approved on the capital plan funded starting July 1; the facilities director favors buying individual mini-split units for staff to install rather than a full building control system to avoid prevailing wage costs.

budget_items.topic: MRPC annual report and grant-writing services
budget_items.what_was_said: Karen and her MRPC team were retained for another stretch covering two years of annual reports and one more grant-writing round.
A Facebook post reported the savings from the street light conversion project using before-and-after cost data provided by the chair.

budget_items.topic: Street light project ROI / purchase cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The town is nearing the payback point on buying the streetlight infrastructure itself (the rest was grant-funded); the purchase price rose during negotiations.
A smaller town converting 30 street lights did not purchase the infrastructure and must keep paying Eversource for maintenance, which was described as roughly half the old cost burden.
The facilities director gave a rough cost for a new building control system for the library, for controls alone; the library does not want mini-splits for aesthetic reasons.
The chair cited an example cost quoted to fix a malfunctioning control device as too high, to argue the facilities director needs better in-house understanding of building control systems.
A prior capital plan figure for cruiser funding was discussed, with a matching purchase expected in 2026 under a plan just approved at town meeting; word is the cruisers came in under budget.
The chair criticized municipal procurement rules, using a hypothetical appropriation to illustrate how vendors tailor bids to whatever budget is announced rather than bidding first.

budget_items.what_was_said: The recycler would charge a fee per pickup to recycle a container held at Hanford.
The container cost is still to be determined, and Tyler is to look for a grant to offset it.
Members discussed a token charge per bag to help fund the system, and keeping it at or below the cost of normal trash bags.
Kim gave the price of the large Lunenburg trash bags as a comparison unit.
If bag revenue exceeds the pickup fee, the container cost could be offset over some number of loads.
A local sponsor or investor might fund the one-time container purchase.
The committee is awaiting word on the grant it applied for, expected around end of February or early March.
A state technical assistance award is available to help identify programs for the next round of grant funding, with an application deadline in March.
Money placed in the earlier budget for grant writing has not been used, and the interim town manager suggested a better use. A full-time grant writer was described as likely to pay for themselves.
Dave described last year's override impact on an average home and how it scales per million, and said capital work has been backed up for years.

what_happened.line: The task force voted unanimously by roll call to authorize the chair to ask the select board to convert two associate seats to alternates and start the process to add Tyler.
Members heard a pilot plan for a styrofoam recycling drop-off at Hanford; the container cost and a per-bag charge are undecided, and Tyler is to look for a grant.
The committee is awaiting word on its fall Green Communities grant, and a state technical assistance application is due in March; the chair will consult the state adviser Kelly first.
Members discussed unused grant-writing money and the tax impact of building projects; no resolution was reached.
The next meeting was set for the first Monday in March, the third, at six o'clock by Zoom.

why_it_matters: The styrofoam drop-off would be paid for partly by a per-bag charge on residents, so the container cost, any grant and the price per bag decide what a household would pay to use it.
The seat change goes to the select board, which decides who may sit on the committee and vote, and the fall grant decision bears on what the town can fund in energy work, including at a school.
